newsitem.title: UK: Tight supply boosts Wet Brent to Aug -19 cts.
newsitem.headline: Tight supply boosts Wet Brent to Aug -19 cts.

text.p: North Sea physical crude markets firmed on Monday when a cargo of benchmark Brent Blend crude changed hands at a sharply stronger August Brent -19 cents, traders said.
Buoyant demand from numerous shorts hauled the value of the July 5-7 loader, over 40 cents above a Brent June 26-28 stem moved at August Brent -60 cents on Tuesday last week.
"It's that surprising. There are so many people who are short out there," said a trader at a European major.
Two Forties, one loading July 9-11 and the other loading 14-16, were also heard changing hands on Monday but no details were immediately available.
Business in other North Sea grades was described as relatively quiet.
The seller of the July 5-7 Brent, originally a Suko equity stem, obtained it on Friday but the level paid was not immediately known.
The wet market was set to continue firm because of the short-term tightness and uncertainty over the destination of Brent cargoes in the hands of a major.

The major was heard to have placed two Brent cargoes into Spain last week and trying to fill a ULCC to move out of the region, although players could not see a profitable sale into the U.S. at current arb levels.
The major declined to comment on the talk.

Concern over new U.N. Security Council threats of sanctions against Iraq continued to firm outright values, traders said, but IPE August futures drifted about eight cents off midday values to $17.88 a barrel at 1541 GMT.
